thread:
Sasha K: Heads-up — thinking about switching a portion of our GPU slots to capacity-optimized spot pools during predictable batch windows to cut interruptions. Planning: 60% capacity-optimized for critical batches, 40% price-optimized for opportunistic experiments. Thoughts?

Matt L: sounds reasonable. curious about the latency-sensitive burst jobs — do we keep an on-demand warm buffer?

Sasha K: yes, proposal includes small always-on on-demand pool for < 100ms cold-start targets. warm buffer size = 3 nodes per region, TTL 10m idle.

Jordan P: agree on mixed pools. nits: price-optimized will save $ but higher churn. we should add fast checkpointing to job runtime so preemptions are cheap. also region spread to avoid correlated evictions.

Liam R: +1. also watch egress and cross-region networking cost if we spread too aggressively. can we prefer AZ diversity inside same region first?

Sasha K: plan: prioritize AZ diversity, then region fallback if capacity brittle. we'll tag workloads with "latency=critical|best-effort" and route accordingly.

Erin V: for autoscaler, how about configuring scale-up policy to prefer capacity-optimized before spinning price-optimized? we can encode bid preference in nodeTemplate. Example k8s nodePool config snippet: 
```yaml
nodePool:
  name: gpu-capacity-optimized
  providerOptions:
    spotStrategy: CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED
  maxSize: 120
  minSize: 10
---
nodePool:
  name: gpu-price-optimized
  providerOptions:
    spotStrategy: PRICE_OPTIMIZED
  maxSize: 200
  minSize: 0
```

Matt L: also consider time-of-day scaling. our weekday midday batch windows are predictable — buy a small short-term reservation for those windows to lower spot churn. predictive windows could be 2–6h reservations.

Jordan P: +1 on short reservations. Another tactic: reduce eviction impact by using local NVMe caching + frequent incremental checkpoints. Put checkpointing in the runtime agent so it's transparent to users.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: new autoscaler policy PR opened by @sasha in repo infra/autoscaler (#427). CI passed.

Liam R: on interruption handling, let's define SLOs: critical jobs tolerate <1% preempted-at-runtime; best-effort tolerate >10%. That will drive how much warm on-demand we keep and how many reserved windows we buy.

Sasha K: good point. i'll draft SLO numbers and a cost vs. availability curve for the next runbook review. Anyone want to own the checkpoint-agent PoC?

Jordan P: I can take PoC. will prototype incremental checkpoints + resumable job API. target prototype in 2 weeks.

Erin V: i'll update autoscaler config and the billing estimation spreadsheet with egress numbers for multi-region fallback.

Sasha K: awesome. next steps: Jordan PoC, Erin autoscaler + cost calc, Sasha runbook with SLOs and reservation windows. thanks :thumbsup: 

Matt L: one more: add alerting for preemption-rate > 3% over 15m for critical pool so ops can intervene.

Sasha K: added to runbook checklist.

InfraBot: incident-bot: no active incidents in the last 72h.

Jordan P: quick question — for GCP preemptible vs AWS spot differences: we should standardize our node abstraction so strategy can be provider-agnostic. I'll include that in the PoC.

Sasha K: yep, abstracting provider spot flags and eviction metadata is in scope. thanks everyone.
